questions.question: A route calls `pbkdf2Sync` with 600,000 iterations. Why does `/health` become slow while it runs?
options: Express queues health checks behind POST requests
Your JavaScript runs on one thread, so synchronous work blocks every other request in the process until it finishes
The health route shares a rate limiter with the hash route
questions.explanation: Express runs your code on a single event-loop thread. A long synchronous computation delays every other request in that process, even trivial ones.

questions.question: Why is switching from `pbkdf2Sync` to the async `pbkdf2` often enough to unblock the main thread?
options: The async version runs on libuv's thread pool instead of the main thread
The async version uses fewer iterations
The async version is cached after the first call
The async version runs inside a worker thread created per request
questions.explanation: Node's async `crypto.pbkdf2`, `crypto.scrypt`, `zlib` and file system calls run on libuv's thread pool (4 threads by default, set with `UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE`). Pure JavaScript work has no async version and needs worker threads.

questions.question: Behind a load balancer with a 60-second idle timeout, what is the recommended `server.keepAliveTimeout` setting?
options: Leave Node's 5-second default so idle sockets are freed quickly
Set it to 0 to disable keep-alive
Set it to 30 seconds, half the load balancer's timeout
Set it longer than the load balancer's idle timeout, such as 65 seconds
questions.explanation: If Node closes idle sockets before the load balancer does, the LB can reuse a closed socket and return intermittent 502s. Making Node outlive the proxy (for example 65,000 ms) avoids this.

questions.question: Why does the lesson use a pool such as `piscina` instead of spawning a new worker thread per request?
options: Worker threads cannot return values without a pool
Spawning a worker costs tens of milliseconds and several MB each, so reusing a pool of workers is far cheaper
Pools let workers share the main thread's event loop
Without a pool, data cannot be passed to the worker
questions.explanation: Creating a worker is slow and memory-hungry. A pool keeps a set of workers alive and reuses them, so each request only pays for the task itself.
